With PATH set, python3 works fine even with an otherwise empty environment ✓. Without PATH, python3 is broken (Python can't determine its prefix without a proper executable path resolution).

So let me harden run.sh: if PATH is unset or doesn't contain a working python3, set a sane default PATH. Cheap insurance:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$DIR"
if [ -z "${PATH:-}" ]; then
  PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
  export PATH
fi
exec python3 -B main.py
```

Even better: verify python3 exists; if not, try known locations. Let me do:

#!/bin/sh
# Entry point for the rule-mining service.
# Reads one JSON request on stdin, writes one JSON response on stdout, exits 0.
set -eu

DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$DIR"

# Make sure an interpreter can be located even with a stripped environment.
if [ -z "${PATH:-}" ]; then
    PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
    export PATH
fi

if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PY=python3
elif [ -x /usr/local/bin/python3 ]; then
    PY=/usr/local/bin/python3
elif [ -x /usr/bin/python3 ]; then
    PY=/usr/bin/python3
else
    PY=python3
fi

exec "$PY" -B main.py
EOF
